changelog: delete C2 — remove a broad, restating principle that overlaps specific attachment-protecting rules so the prompt can concentrate on concrete, testable bindings (responding to the critique that predicate–complement protection needs focused rules and to the 'prune' constraint).
findings: The prompt under-protects predicate–complement attachments: it permits cuts that separate a verb/auxiliary/copula from the essential complement (object, PP, numeral/parenthetical, or named-location) that completes its meaning, producing contradictions or orphan fragments when pieces are translated independently.

edits.was: - If the pieces are translated independently and concatenated, will the joined t

diagnosis.why: Removing C2 weakened the prompt's broad, restating protection for predicate–complement and head-dependent spans, so the model began allowing more aggressive, fine-grained cuts (helping very-short pieces: ≤3 bin +0.0117 and producing a slight net of more improvements overall) while increasing harmful mid-clause/head splits in medium-length chunks (≤10 bin −0.005), which produced the large negative tail moves that break noun/verb or enumerated-unit integrity.
diagnosis.lesson: Keep an explicit, high-level constraint that protects predicate–complement and head-dependent integrity so the prompt does not encourage splitting inside phrases in medium-length pieces.
